chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu Al-Rabie, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about the Sa'ibah, so he said: 'He is the man who emancipates his slave, then says to him, “Go wherever you wish. There is nothing from your inheritance for me, nor is there upon me from your crimes anything,” and he should have two witnesses testify to that.'
ai.seo_question: What is the definition and legal ruling of Sa'ibah in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific legal mechanism of 'Saibah' emancipation, where the master explicitly severs both financial inheritance ties and blood-guilt liability (daman al-jarirah) through a witnessed declaration. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the master's unilateral intent and the necessity of two witnesses to formalize this complete severance of kinship-like bonds, distinguishing it from conditional manumission.
